Rebuilding the included iPhone 3G ARMv6 executables

Build-only requirements: macOS with Xcode clang and codesign, Python 3, make,
and a separately obtained iPhoneOS4.2.sdk. End users do not need these tools.
No SDK, firmware, or proprietary runtime library is redistributed in this bundle.

1. Build cctools-port inside a local build directory:

   git clone https://github.com/tpoechtrager/cctools-port.git
   git -C cctools-port checkout df82634ce7c3eddba9722e881433fbe357396e16
   git -C cctools-port apply /absolute/path/to/ld64-host-page-size.patch
   cd cctools-port/cctools
   ./configure --build=aarch64-apple-darwin27 --host=aarch64-apple-darwin27 --prefix="$PWD/../install" --target=arm-apple-darwin10 --disable-tapi-support --disable-xar-support
   make -j8
   make install

   The explicit aarch64 host/build values were necessary on this Apple Silicon
   host because this older project's config.guess incorrectly classified it as
   32-bit ARM. On Intel Macs, use the correct host/build identifiers instead.
   The prefix above stays inside the checkout; no system tool installation occurs.

2. From this source bundle directory, run:

   python3 build_payloads.py --sdk /absolute/path/to/iPhoneOS4.2.sdk --linker /absolute/path/to/cctools-port/install/bin/arm-apple-darwin10-ld --clang /absolute/path/to/clang

   This was validated with Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2). Modern Apple's
   ld no longer links ARMv6 even when its version output lists ARMv6, hence the
   isolated legacy linker. -mlinker-version=609 suppresses new linker flags.
   The repeated platform-version warning is expected: the explicit final value
   records minimum iOS 4.0 and SDK 4.2 even when modern clang cannot read the old
   SDKSettings.plist. The ignored current compiler-runtime archive warning is
   expected; every required division helper resolves to the ramdisk's libgcc_s.1.

3. The output directory contains bruteforce, device_infos, restored_external,
   and SHA256.json. All three are compiled for ARM1176JZF-S (ARMv6) and use the
   legacy LC_UNIXTHREAD entry point. No binary architecture headers are patched.

   SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is fixed to the pinned source commit's timestamp. Two clean
   builds with the recorded compiler/linker on this host produced identical files.
   The payload source changes remove automatic fsck_hfs repair from
   restored_external add a bounded --sleep SECONDS mode, and update a read-only HFS /dev/md0 root
   directly through mount(2). The modified source is already present in source/. The
   original file is retained in original/ramdisk_tools/, and the exact patch is
   payload-no-auto-fsck.patch. All other payload sources and Apple open source
   headers are unchanged. SOURCE-MANIFEST.json covers both original and modified
   files. All original notices remain present; the revision suffix
   +no-auto-fsck identifies this application build.

4. codesign adds ad-hoc signatures with SHA1 as the primary CodeDirectory and
   SHA256 as an alternate, plus the original project's XML entitlements. SHA1 is
   needed by the old iOS kernel. Current codesign refuses SHA1-only signatures.
   Strict codesign verification and independent SHA1/SHA256 page-hash checks passed.

Validation scope

These files are built for an iOS 4 restore environment and are not compatible
with a 3.1.3 ramdisk. All strong imports (127, 124 and 157 respectively) were
checked against the actual ARMv6 libraries from Apple's iPhone1,2 4.2.1 8C148
restore ramdisk. VALIDATION.json records exact firmware/library hashes and
signature results. Source/kernel compatibility still requires the matching
4.2.1 ramdisk and the kernel patches supplied by the host application's adapter.
No iPhone execution, ramdisk boot, or physical-device recovery has been tested.

Automatic repair policy

The application does not automatically run filesystem repair. The restored_external
payload waits for the data partition without invoking fsck_hfs. Its USB setup is retained.
The RAM root helper checks statfs, requires an HFS /dev/md0 root, and skips
an already writable root. A required read-only-to-writable update uses mount(2)
with the pinned XNU hfs_mount_args header. This avoids mount_hfs reopening the
mounted block device and emitting GetMasterBlock EBUSY (16). Ownership, encoding,
permissions and timezone are retained. Failed or ineffective updates stop startup.
The original mountDataPartition implementation
used by bruteforce mounts the data partition with MNT_RDONLY. Kernel NAND boot
arguments were not changed to implement this policy.

Bundled wait helper

The selected legacy SSH archive and 4.2.1 restore image do not provide an external
sleep utility. The restored_external source therefore includes --sleep SECONDS,
accepting only ASCII decimal 0..3600 and repeating interrupted libc sleep calls.
This mode returns before watchdog, USB, device information or filesystem access.
The host adapter installs a separate verified bundled copy as
/usr/local/bin/bl-ios-wait, including when custom recovery payloads are selected.
The managed script uses this helper for its readiness and hold delays. If the
helper is absent or fails, its hold path stops itself with the shell kill builtin
instead of spinning. The new helper logic passed isolated native-host C tests;
its ARMv6 code signatures and actual firmware imports were independently checked.
